surface_summary: Hartley Parrish is found dead in his locked library with a pistol in hand, apparently a suicide. Voices were heard in the library shortly before the shot, and a mysterious letter from a Rotterdam firm suggests blackmail. Suspicion falls on Robin Greve, who denies visiting Parrish, but the truth is obscured by conflicting testimonies and missing evidence.
accepted_facts: Hartley Parrish was found dead with a pistol in his hand in a locked library.
A shot was heard by Mary Trevert at about 5:15 PM.
Bude the butler heard voices in the library shortly before the shot.
A letter on slatey-blue paper from Elias van der Spyck & Co. was found on Parrish’s desk.
inferred_conclusions: Robin Greve visited Parrish and had a heated argument with him.
Parrish committed suicide due to business worries and nervous condition.
The shot heard was the only shot fired and was self-inflicted.
mechanism_description: Albert Edward Jeekes, acting under orders from Victor Marbran, confronted Hartley Parrish at the open library window with a pistol identical to Parrish’s. Parrish fired a silenced shot at Jeekes, who returned fire with a loud shot that killed Parrish. Jeekes then staged the scene as a suicide by placing Parrish’s pistol without the silencer in his hand and closing the window. He escaped through the window, taking care to avoid leaving marks, and later confessed before dying by suicide.
delivery_path: Jeekes approaches Parrish at the open library window with a Browning pistol.
Parrish fires a silenced shot at Jeekes, missing him.
Jeekes fires a loud shot that kills Parrish instantly.
Jeekes places Parrish’s pistol without the silencer in Parrish’s hand.
Jeekes closes the window to simulate a suicide scene.
Jeekes escapes through the window, avoiding leaving footprints or marks.
Jeekes later writes a confession and kills himself.
outcome_result: Jeekes is revealed as the murderer acting under Marbran’s orders and confesses before dying by suicide.

false_assumption.statement: The death of Hartley Parrish was a straightforward suicide caused by business worries.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Parrish was found with a pistol in his hand and medical evidence indicated instantaneous death by a gunshot to the heart. The presence of a threatening letter and his nervous condition suggested a motive for suicide.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that Parrish was murdered by Jeekes who used a silenced shot and staged the scene to look like suicide, misleading the police and witnesses.

supporting_points: Bude testified hearing voices in the library shortly after Greve passed him.
Greve had a known rivalry and confrontation with Parrish over Mary Trevert.
Greve was unaccounted for during the time of the murder and had opportunity.
Greve’s denial of visiting Parrish was contradicted by servants’ testimony.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Greve had a solid alibi and no physical evidence linked him to the murder; the voices heard were misattributed and the real culprit was Jeekes.

red_herrings.description: Robin Greve is suspected due to his argument with Parrish and the butler hearing voices after he passed.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Greve did not enter the library and the voices were from Jeekes and Parrish during the murder.

red_herrings.description: Mary Trevert’s engagement to Parrish and her previous relationship with Greve create suspicion and emotional motives.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Mary was a witness and had no motive or opportunity; Greve was innocent and wrongly suspected.

closed_circle.rationale: All had access to Harkings and potential motives or opportunity, but investigation and evidence narrowed the culprit to Jeekes acting under Marbran’s orders.

discriminating_test.design: Reconstruct the murder scene at Harkings library with the window open and the silencer removed from the pistol. Test whether the sounds of two shots, one silenced and one loud, can be heard and whether the murderer could have escaped through the window without leaving marks. Confirm the presence of two pistols of identical caliber and the timing of voices and shots.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that two shots were fired, the silenced shot first by Parrish, then the loud shot by the murderer, and that the murderer escaped through the open window, staging the scene as suicide.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The test passes if the timing and acoustic conditions match witness testimonies and physical evidence, and if the escape through the window is plausible without leaving footprints or marks.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all essential clues: the locked library door, the open window, the missing silencer, the coded letter, the testimony of Bude and Mary Trevert, and the discovery of the bullet mark on the rosery tree. The conflicting testimonies and the presence of two pistols are highlighted. The confession letter is foreshadowed and the decoding of the letter is explained. The reader can deduce the murder disguised as suicide by analyzing the timing of the shots and the physical evidence.
